messages:
marta: Quick heads up — I'm seeing a discrepancy in the hourly aggregate for `route:usage` between OLAP and the Console. Window 2026-02-11 03:00–04:00 shows ~9% fewer tokens in OLAP vs Console.
raj: Can you paste the query and sample shard ids?
marta: Query: `SELECT hour, sum(tokens) FROM telemetry.agg_route_usage WHERE hour='2026-02-11T03' GROUP BY hour;` Sample shards: s-42, s-43, s-78.
oliver: FYI our late-ingest sweep logged an error on s-43 around that interval — parquet writer retried and dropped a file due to manifest mismatch (see logs). Might explain missing rows.
amanda: That was during the autoscaler incident when we hit the parquet write quota and the backfill was canceled. Job id `af_backfill_20260211_01`. I can pull the job logs.
kevin: Important: before we do any full reprocess we should run a checksum-by-event-id pass to avoid double-counting if we end up re-ingesting partially-processed batches. Suggest dry-run flag `--idempotency=event_id` and `--verify-only`.
analytics-bot: quick-check: ran parity diff for route:usage on s-42,s-43 — mismatches: s-43: 9.2% short, s-42: 0.1%, s-78: 0.0%. Checksum diff file: s3://redwood-telemetry/parity/2026-02-11/shard-checksums.csv
raj: OK. Proposed plan: 1) small canary reprocess on s-43 for the hour window with `--verify-only` and generate checksums; 2) if checksums match Console, run idempotent reprocess; 3) run aggregate reconciliation job; 4) promote to other affected shards. Thoughts?
marta: +1. Add an intermediate step to verify parquet manifests and tombstones so we don't try to re-ingest files that were intentionally tombstoned. Also record a manifest snapshot before reprocess.
oliver: Implementation notes: airflow dag `telemetry.reprocess_v2` supports `--shard` and `--dry-run`. I can add a `--manifest-snapshot` flag that writes a small manifest to s3. Command example:
```
python infra/tools/reprocess.py --start 2026-02-11T03:00 --end 2026-02-11T04:00 --shard s-43 --idempotency event_id --verify-only --manifest-snapshot s3://redwood-telemetry/canary-manifests/1805001234.json
```
This will produce checksums and a dry-run report.
amanda: I'll schedule the canary tonight at 22:30 PST (after low traffic), will set retention to 7d and attach logs to the run ticket.
kevin: Also we need SRE approval for increased IO during wide replays; open a short change ticket so SRE knows expected bytes/sec and concurrency.
sre-bot: CHANGE REQUEST CREATED: CR-2026-118 — expected peak 450 MB/s for 20m window, approval pending.
raj: If canary looks good, we should use the job-level `--concurrency=2` and lane it through dedicated reproc pool to minimize impact. Also enable `--skip-cache=true` so we don't accidentally pull stale cached prefixes.
marta: Good. I'll own the reconciliation step (compare final aggregated numbers, run `agg_diff` script, and create a rollback plan if mismatch > 0.5%).
amanda: I'll post the run ticket in #incidents and ping here when canary completes. Will also attach the dry-run checksums and manifest snapshot. :thumbsup:
analytics-bot: Post-canary report stub (auto): parity_pass=false, checksum_delta=9.2%, details_url=s3://redwood-telemetry/parity/reports/1805001234-report.json
kevin: If parity_pass=false we abort and do a deeper parquet-level repair (vacuum + rebuild manifest) — that was painful last time, let's avoid by starting with manifest snapshot.
marta: Thanks all — schedule looks set. Amanda, ping when the dry-run report is uploaded and then we'll decide next step.
amanda: Roger. Scheduling now.
sre-bot: JOB SCHEDULED: airflow run telemetry.reprocess_v2 af_backfill_20260211_01 (canary) at 2026-03-02T22:30:00-08:00
